name: ON Semiconductor Corporation
moat_justification: Genuine leadership positions (SiC, auto image sensing) with long automotive qualification cycles and vertical integration, but semiconductors sell into cyclical end markets with aggressive scaled rivals and Chinese SiC entrants, and FY2023-25 proved onsemi has no pricing power strong enough to hold margins through a downturn — it took $667M of restructuring/impairment charges and cut ~2,400 jobs instead.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.8%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Quality cyclical power/sensing franchise, moat 5/10 — the recovery is real but already paid for: weighted IRR 8.4%, IV@15 $32.81 vs $72.10 price; it clears 15% only near $33.
moat_for: Vertically integrated SiC chain (boule to module), ~24% global SiC share, 200mm transition under way
Long auto design-win/qualification cycles create switching friction
AI data-center power revenue ramping (guided to more than double in 2026)
moat_against: Deeply cyclical: revenue fell from $8,326M (FY2022) to $5,995M (FY2025), margins collapsed with utilization
SiC price competition from STMicroelectronics, Infineon, and Chinese entrants
Auto + industrial ~75% of sales — two end markets drive everything
Fab-heavy cost structure: downturns become impairments, not just lower margins
